claims.text: Standard APS-produced AlCoCrFeNi coatings exhibit a moderately coarse grain-size distribution.
Changing plasma temperature and spray distance can increase the cooling rate during APS deposition.
A higher cooling rate during APS deposition produces a finer grain structure in AlCoCrFeNi coatings.
Cooling rate is the only intended variable, while coating composition and environmental conditions remain constant.
Higher cooling rates induce more rapid solidification.
Rapid solidification produces a finer microstructure.
Rapid solidification produces a more homogeneous microstructure.
A finer and more homogeneous microstructure increases coating hardness.
A finer and more homogeneous microstructure limits wear-induced crack propagation.
A finer and more homogeneous microstructure acts as a barrier to particle penetration.
AlCoCrFeNi coatings with finer grains will have higher hardness than standard APS coatings.
AlCoCrFeNi coatings with finer grains will have lower wear rates than standard APS coatings.
Standard APS parameters typically produce coarser AlCoCrFeNi coatings with lower wear resistance.
The proposed cooling-rate effect should hold over the range of APS parameters typical for AlCoCrFeNi coatings.
Excessive oxide formation or secondary-phase formation may introduce wear effects beyond those attributable to grain refinement.

contradictions.description: The conditions state that only cooling rate is varied, but the intervention changes plasma temperature and spray distance. Those process parameters can independently alter particle heating, oxidation, porosity, deposition efficiency, and splat formation, so cooling rate is not demonstrably the sole changed variable.
